penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Diagnosing and fixing Einstein Recipe misconfiguration requires access to the specific Marketing Cloud org, data schema, and recipe settings — per-customer manual investigation is necessary for any meaningful deliverable beyond generic documentation.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Marketing ops teams in enterprise SFMC environments expect iterative back-and-forth to resolve configuration issues — a one-shot automated output is insufficient.

rationale: Marketing operations professionals at mid-market and enterprise companies using SFMC are strong buyers — SFMC licenses are expensive and these teams have budgets for consulting and tooling. However, like the OmniScript opportunity, meaningful help requires hands-on access to each customer's specific MCP configuration, data categories, and recipe settings; Claude cannot autonomously debug this from the outside. A generic troubleshooting guide exists (Salesforce docs), so the value of an automated checklist is limited. The penalty-adjusted total drops well below the validate threshold. Drop unless a very narrow self-serve audit tool (no org access, pure questionnaire-driven) can realistically surface value.
solution_plan: This is not viable as a fully automated service — debugging Einstein Recipes requires org access and iterative testing that a non-technical operator cannot do. A self-serve 'SFMC Personalization Diagnostic Guide' (structured questionnaire → Claude-generated action plan → PDF, ~$49) is the closest viable form, similar to the OmniScript opportunity above. Build: Claude prompt covering known Einstein Recipe category-filter failure modes + intake form + automated delivery + Stripe. Sell: target SFMC-focused communities (Salesforce Trailblazer, MarTech forums) with a free sample. Maintain: automated. Honest caveat: the addressable market for this specific niche is small and the willingness to pay $49 for a checklist (vs just asking on Stack Exchange for free) is unproven. Only worth building if the OmniScript variant validates first and shows cross-sell potential.
